summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted for septic shock due to a Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection. He presented with hypotension, leukocytosis, and acute kidney injury following a blocked Foley catheter. He was treated in the ICU with IV fluids, dopamine, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, then transitioned to ceftriaxone once culture results were available. His renal function and blood pressure normalized, and he was weaned off vasopressors. Pain and neuropsychiatric medications were held initially due to drug interactions but were safely restarted. He improved clinically, completed a course of IV antibiotics, and was discharged to extended care with plans to finish treatment and monitor INR.
